I've saved the Q3 answers to `/work/answer.json`. With the same rules applied to Q2, the script reproduces all 10 reference values exactly.

| 항목 | 3분기 결과 |
|---|---|
| a. 순매출 1위 세그먼트 | consumer, 361,812,421원 |
| b. 결제 완료 주문이 있는 고객 수 | 244명 |
| c. 순매출 1위 카테고리 | svc, 295,931,623원 |
| d. 순매출이 가장 큰 달 | 2025-09 |
| e. 환불액 합계 1위 고객 | u4@ex.com |
| f. 결제 완료 주문 2건 이상 고객 수 | 228명 |
| g. 주문당 평균 순매출 | 702,814원 |
| h. 8월 대비 9월 증가율 | 14.1% |

To match the Q2 reference, I had to apply two rules that weren't in your definitions:

1. **Order dates are read in Korean time (UTC+9).** `ordered_at` is stored in UTC with a `Z` suffix. Without converting to Korean time, 7 of the 10 Q2 values don't match, because orders placed late in the evening UTC fall on the next day, and some move into the next month or quarter.
2. **Customers are counted by email, not by customer ID.** The `customers` table has 300 rows but only 250 distinct emails, so some customers appear more than once. I compare emails with letter case and surrounding spaces ignored, and this affects b, e and f. With the times converted but customers counted by ID, Q2 gives b=281 and f=223 instead of the reference 236 and 199.

I also normalized `segment` values, which have mixed letter case and stray spaces (for example ` consumer` and `Enterprise `). Refunds were matched to order lines by order and product. All refunds match an existing order line, and none exceeds the quantity ordered.

STATUS: DONE
